parsed.summary: PLAN-B74 has rigorously addressed all prior feedback from Gemini and Groq: statistical safeguards against look-ahead bias (strict completed daily bar pivots, confirm date offset, out-of-sample analog factor freeze), overlapping return handling (monthly block bootstrap), Elliott wave hard rules and corrections (flats + zigzags, explicit unclassified state), multi-hypothesis FDR control (overall BH + 4-subperiod sign consistency), database date normalization, and LLM circuit breakers/price validators are all well-specified. The plan is technically sound, methodologically honest, and safe to execute.

findings.issue: At 08:20 pre-market scheduled run, Asian markets (N225, KS11) have opened at 08:00 TST and Yahoo daily bars may return an incomplete intraday candle for day T, while US indices (SOX, IXIC, GSPC) represent fully completed day T-1 candles. Computing 1/5/20-day returns with mixed incomplete/complete bars can distort correlation and relative strength.
findings.suggestion: Explicitly specify in globalx.py that at 08:20, non-TW Asian index daily series use completed T-1 session closes (or filter out partial bars where bar date == today) to maintain temporal consistency with US indices.

findings.issue: Section 4.2 phrases wave 2 hard rule as '第 2 浪不跌破第 1 浪起點', which assumes an upward impulse. For downward impulse waves (e.g., wave C impulse or broad downtrends), wave 2 must not rally above wave 1 start and wave 4 must not rise into wave 1 price territory.
findings.suggestion: Ensure the rule checker in engine.py parameterizes wave boundaries symmetrically for both bullish and bearish impulses (e.g. Wave 2 does not retrace beyond 100% of Wave 1 in the counter-trend direction).

findings.issue: In support/resistance hold rate evaluation, if a single volatile day t touches a support level (Low <= Level) and simultaneously experiences an intraday swing where High >= Level + 1*ATR and Close < Level - 0.5*ATR, daily bar data lacks tick-level sequence to prove which threshold was hit first.
findings.suggestion: Define a deterministic tie-breaker in R1/R2 rules: e.g., if touched and same-day close is below breakdown threshold, count as failure; or explicitly track subsequent outcome starting from t+1.

parsed.coverage: Reviewed all 12 sections of PLAN-B74, including UI/UX changes, database schema & migrations, ZigZag pivot confirmation logic, Elliott wave hard rules & soft scoring, support/resistance clustering, chips & global index integration, analog forecasting calibration (R1-R6), LLM roundtable multi-provider architecture, Telegram push formatting, test scripts, and operational failover mechanics.
parsed.limitations: Review is based on architecture and algorithm design specifications in the plan document; execution runtime performance and third-party API availability (FinMind, Groq, Fly.io networking) will require monitoring in staging/production.
